When you create a table, you need to specify a name for the table (.dbf) file created to store the table. Both database tables and free tables require table file names. Table names must begin with a letter or underscore and can consist of letters, digits, or underscores.

If your table is in a database, you can specify a long table name, which can contain up to 128 characters, in addition to the table file name. You can use long table names instead of conventional file names to identify the table in a database more easily. [[T0]] displays long table names when the table appears in the [[T1]] interface, for example in the Project Manager, the Database Designer, the Query Designer, and the View Designer as well as in the title bar of a browse window.

> **Note:** If you remove a table from a database, the table retains its file name but not its long name.

- Open the database table in the Table Designer .
- In the Table Designer , click the Table tab.
- In the Name box, type a long name for the table.

- Include the [[T0]] clause when creating a database table with the [[T1]] command.

For more information, see Table Designer ([[T2]]) and [[T3]] - [[T4]] Command.

You can rename the long names for database tables and the file names of database and free tables. You can rename the long names of database tables using the Table Designer because you are changing the long name, not the table file name. You can rename free tables only programmatically because free tables do not have long names.

- Open the database in the Database Designer .
- Find and make the table you want to rename active.
- On the Database menu, click Modify .
- In the Table Designer , click the Table tab.
- In the Name box, type a new name for the table.

For more information, see Database Designer ([[T0]]) and Table Designer ([[T1]]).

- Set the database containing the table you want to rename as the current database.
- Use the [[T0]] command.

For more information, see [[T1]] Command.

- Use the [[T0]] command. Caution Do not use the [[T1]] command on database tables. [[T2]] does not update the table's back link to the database and might cause errors when accessing the table. Use the [[T3]] command instead.

For more information, see [[T4]] Command.

Makes it possible for you to select fields.

When this dialog box opens by selecting Only fields specified by field filter and then clicking Field Filter in the Work Area Properties dialog box, this dialog box makes it possible for you to select fields that display or can be accessed in a browse window. Copies the selected fields from the All Fields box to the Selected Fields box.
**All**
Copies all fields from the All Fields box to the Selected Fields box.
**Remove**
Removes the selected fields from the Selected Fields box.

When you build a project, application, or dynamic-link library, [[T0]] includes build status and error messages in an error file, which is a text file with the .err file name extension, as they occur during the build process. The .err file has the same base name as your project and is created in the current directory. When you compile or recompile a project, application, or dynamic-link library, compile messages are also included in the same .err file.

If the build process is interrupted, you can open the .err file to review these messages. You can also select the Display Errors option in the Build Options dialog box to display an editing window for the .err file after the build process completes so you can review any errors.

> **Note:** If no errors occur during the build, the .err file is removed.

During the build process, build status messages appear in the status bar. After the build process completes, the number of build errors appear in the status bar.

- Build the project, application, or dynamic-link library file by following the steps in How to: Test a Project or How to: Build Applications .
- To display the error file automatically after the build process completes, when the Build Options dialog box is open, select the Display Errors check box. -[[T0]]- To view the error file after the build process completes, on the Project menu, choose Errors .

For more information, see Build Options Dialog Box.

You can also specify whether to include compile messages by using the [[T1]] command. For more information, see [[T2]] Command.

You can also view and save build status messages that appear in the Debug Output window when it is open in the Debugger. For more information, see Debug Output Window and Debugger Window.

- Build the project, application, or dynamic-link library file by following the steps in How to: Test a Project or How to: Build Applications , respectively.
- In the Build Options dialog box, select the Recompile All Files check box.
